Gauss-Newton linearized least-squares step with QR/SVD rank safeguards
Finite-budget Levenberg-Marquardt with a trust-ratio safeguard
Gauss-Newton contracts linearly under a controlled residual-curvature bound
items.statement:
Let $m,n\ge1$, and let $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^2$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let
$\phi=\|r\|_2^2/2$, $J=Dr$, $A=J^TJ$, and
$S(x)=\sum_i r_i(x)\nabla^2r_i(x)$. Let $x_*\in U$ satisfy
$J(x_*)^Tr(x_*)=0$, and let the closed ball
$B=\{x:\|x-x_*\|_2\le R\}$ lie in $U$, with $R>0$. Suppose on $B$:

- $J(x)$ has full column rank and smallest singular value at least $\sigma>0$;
- $\|J(x)\|_2\le M$;
- $J$ is $L$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean induced matrix norm;
- $\|S(x)\|_2\le\kappa$.

Define $q=(\kappa+MLR)/\sigma^2$ and assume $q<1$. For the exact full-rank
Gauss-Newton step $p(x)=-A(x)^{-1}J(x)^Tr(x)$, supply an exact reduced QR
factorization of $J(x)$ to the exact branch of
[[alg-gauss-newton-qr-svd-step-with-rank-safeguard]] at each $x\in B$; the
full-column-rank hypothesis guarantees such a factorization. Every $x\in B$ satisfies
$$\|x+p(x)-x_*\|_2\le q\|x-x_*\|_2.$$
Consequently the exact iterates from any $x_0\in B$ stay in $B$ and converge
to $x_*$ at a linear rate no larger than $q$. The curvature hypothesis
controls the residual term $S$; no quadratic rate is claimed when it is
nonzero.

items.title: Gauss-Newton converges quadratically at a full-rank zero-residual root
items.statement:
Let $m,n\ge1$, and let $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and let
$x_*\in U$ satisfy $r(x_*)=0$. Let $B=\{x:\|x-x_*\|_2\le R\}\subseteq U$ be
convex. Suppose $J=Dr$ is $L$-Lipschitz on $B$ and, for some $\sigma>0$,
$$\|J(x)v\|_2\ge\sigma\|v\|_2\qquad(x\in B,\ v\in\mathbb R^n).$$
Thus every $J(x)$ has full column rank. For the exact Gauss-Newton iteration
$x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k$, where $p_k$ is the unique minimizer of
$\|r(x_k)+J(x_k)p\|_2^2$. When the iteration uses the exact branch of
[[alg-gauss-newton-qr-svd-step-with-rank-safeguard]], assume each invocation is
supplied with an exact reduced QR factorization of $J(x_k)$. Set
$C=L/(2\sigma)$. Then every $x_k\in B$ satisfies
$$\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|_2\le C\|x_k-x_*\|_2^2.$$
If $C>0$ and $\|x_0-x_*\|_2\le\min\{R,1/(2C)\}$, all iterates stay in the ball,
converge to $x_*$, and contract at least by $1/2$ per iteration after the
quadratic estimate. If $C=0$ and $x_0\in B$, one exact step reaches $x_*$. This result concerns
exact solves; it asserts no finite-precision convergence rate.

title: Gauss newton and levenberg marquardt methods — Examples

items.title: An exponential-decay kinetics fit has a full-rank exact solution
items.statement:
Fit the one-rate exponential-decay model $y(t;a,k)=ae^{-kt}$ to observations at
$t=0$ and $t=1$ with values $2$ and $2e^{-1}$. Its residual is
$r(a,k)=(a-2,\;ae^{-k}-2e^{-1})^T$. The parameter $x_*=(2,1)$ is an exact fit,
and the Jacobian there has full column rank. Thus the exact full-rank
Gauss-Newton step at $x_*$ is zero. This is a local exact-fit illustration; it
does not claim that a nonlinear iteration from every initial parameter
converges to $x_*$.

items.title: Rank-deficient data do not identify both parameters, while LM has a unique damped step
items.statement:
Let $r(a,b)=(a+b-1,\;2(a+b-1))^T$. The data depend only on $a+b$, so they do
not identify $a$ and $b$ separately. At $(0,0)$ the Gauss-Newton Jacobian is
rank deficient and its linearized least-squares problem has many minimizers.
With $D=I$, damping $\lambda=1$ gives a unique trial step. For trust radius
$\Delta=1$, ratio thresholds $\eta_1=1/4,\eta_2=3/4$, lower damping
$\lambda_{\min}=1/2$, update factor $\gamma=2$, and one allowed trial, that
step is accepted with ratio $1$.
